title: World Cup visitors to U.S. ‘vulnerable to serious harm’, civil rights organisations warn
content:
More than 120 civil society organisations and MLS and NWSL-affiliated fan groups have sent a travel advisory to potential visitors to the United States ahead of this summer’s World Cup, warning that those from immigrant communities, racial and ethnic minority groups, and LGBTQ+ individuals are “most vulnerable to serious harm” when travelling within the country due to government policies.

The advisory, published Thursday, is directed towards fans, players, journalists, and other visitors, calling upon each individual to “exercise caution and have an emergency contingency plan” amidst what they term as the “Trump administration’s rising authoritarianism and increasing violence”.

Evidence cited as part of their advisory includes 48 deaths in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody since the beginning of 2025, total or partial restrictions on entries for visitors from 39 countries, and the presence of ICE agents at airports across the U.S. over recent months.

Amongst the signatories to the letter are Amnesty International USA, Reporters Without Borders, the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), and 20 US-based MLS and NWSL-affiliated supporters’ groups. The total includes organisations from each of the World Cup’s 11 host cities.

Though concerns existed over travel to both the 2018 World Cup in Russia and the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, owing to each nation’s human rights records, it is highly unusual for such warnings to come from such a large number of civil rights organisations within the host country itself.

Both FIFA and the White House rejected these concerns in statements to The Athletic.

They advise that visitors secure electronic devices by removing sensitive information and turning off facial recognition or fingerprint passwords, as well as alerting friends and family of their exact itinerary.

“FIFA has been paying lip service to human rights while cozying up with the Trump administration, putting millions of people at risk of being harmed and their basic rights violated,” said Jamil Dakwar, human rights program director at the ACLU, one of the most historic progressive civil litigation groups in the U.S. “The Trump administration’s abusive actions continue to threaten our communities, tourists, and fans alike — and it’s past time that FIFA uses its leverage to push for meaningful policy changes and binding assurances that will make people feel safe to travel and enjoy the games.”

“The specter of immigration enforcement this summer has become the leading concern among grassroots organisations across host cities,” said Jennifer Li, who leads Dignity 2026, a national coalition working with grassroots groups in host cities, which counts multiple signatories among its members.

“Irrespective of their focus area — housing, labour, immigration — this issue has become a galvanising topic. With less than two months to go, we are still waiting for public commitments from FIFA and host city organisers about plans to protect residents, workers, and visitors. The silence has been deafening.”

In response, a FIFA spokesperson pointed to the organisation’s human rights strategy, stating that: “As per article 3 of the FIFA Statutes, FIFA is committed to respecting all internationally recognised human rights and shall strive to promote the protection of these rights.

“The development and publication of the FWC2026 Sustainability and Human Rights Strategy, the FWC2026 Human Rights Framework, and the recently updated FIFA Statement on Human Rights Defenders and Media Representatives as well as the establishment of an FWC2026 Human Rights Advisory Group comprised of independent experts and the wide advertisement of the FIFA Human Rights Grievance Mechanism, are all evidence of FIFA’s commitment to human rights across all key activities and actors connected to the tournament.”

Representatives from Trump’s administration and the White House’s World Cup Task Force strongly pushed back at any suggestion questioning the tournament’s safety.

“Under President Trump’s leadership, the White House World Cup Task Force has worked relentlessly to ensure the 2026 World Cup will be the most incredible sporting event in U.S. history,” said Andrew Giuliani, executive director of the White House’s World Cup Task Force.

“Our commitment to excellence, safety, and an outstanding experience for every visitor is unmatched. As a global leader in human rights, the United States is prepared to welcome eager travellers from around the world to celebrate the World Cup and America’s 250th birthday together. Our preparations are on track to support FIFA in delivering the greatest World Cup ever! These absurd claims cannot change the reality that the United States is fully prepared to set a new standard for international sporting events.”

Davis Ingle, a White House spokesperson, added: “The FIFA 2026 World Cup will no doubt be one of the greatest and most spectacular events in the history of mankind, attracting millions of fans from around the world to eleven host cities across America.

“This will be a monumental event that requires close coordination between the Trump Administration, FIFA, and all of our great federal, state, and local partners. President Trump is focused on ensuring that this is not only an incredible experience for all fans and visitors, but that it is also the safest and most secure in history — and no amount of ridiculous scare tactics driven by liberal activist groups and the left-wing media will change that.”

Last week, The Athletic reported that senior FIFA officials had discussed the possibility of the organisation’s president, Gianni Infantino, making a direct request to Trump for a full suspension on ICE raids across the United States during the World Cup this summer.

Previously, ICE leadership had stated that the body would play a “key part” across the World Cup, primarily focusing on Homeland Security investigations. However, concerns have been raised by both members of the U.S. Congress and unions that their activities may extend to immigration-enforcement raids which target World Cup events.

Fans at last summer’s Club World Cup in the U.S. alleged sightings of Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and ICE officials at stadiums during the tournament. In a previous statement to The Athletic, a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) spokesperson denied that ICE and CBP conducted enforcement, describing it as “another case of fear-mongering”.
